questions.q: In the accounting equation, what are liabilities and equity?
options: Liabilities are cash; equity is inventory
Liabilities are sales; equity is expenses
Liabilities are what the business owes; equity is the part that belongs to the owner
They are two names for the same thing
questions.evidence: Liabilities are what it owes, and equity is the amount of the company that belongs to the business owner.

options: Formal reports on a company's financial position, cash inflows and outflows, and results of operations
questions.explain: They include the balance sheet, income statement and statement of cash flows.
questions.evidence: These financial statements are formal reports providing information on a company’s financial position, cash inflows and outflows, and the results of operations.

questions.q: Financial statements used by external entities are prepared using…
questions.explain: Common rules make statements comparable between companies.
questions.evidence: Financial statements used by external entities are prepared using Generally Accepted Accounting Principles

questions.q: Under accrual basis accounting, when are revenue and expenses recorded?
options: When revenue is earned and expenses are incurred, regardless of when payment is received
At the end of the year only
questions.explain: Cash basis records them when payment is received or made.
questions.evidence: Revenue is recorded when it is earned and expenses are recorded when they are incurred, regardless of when payment is received.

questions.q: In double-entry bookkeeping, on which side are debits recorded?
options: On the left (credits are on the right)
On the right (credits are on the left)
questions.explain: Every transaction has equal debits and credits.
questions.evidence: debits are on the left and credits are on the right

options: The categories used to track the financial information that is important to us
questions.explain: Examples include Cash, Accounts Receivable, Revenue and Supplies.
questions.evidence: Accounts are the categories that we use to track the financial information that is important to us.

questions.q: What is a journal in bookkeeping?
options: A summary of balances by account
A chronological list of economic events (transactions)
questions.explain: Entries are later posted to the ledger, which sorts them by account.
questions.evidence: it is still a chronological list of economic events (transactions)

questions.q: When are adjusting journal entries made?
options: At the end of an accounting period, or whenever financial statements are prepared, so revenues and expenses match
Only when there is an error
questions.explain: Adjustments apply the matching principle of accrual accounting.
questions.evidence: adjusting journal entries are made at the end of an accounting period or any time financial statements are prepared so that we have matching revenues and expenses.

questions.q: In the closing process, where are the credit balances of revenue accounts transferred?
options: To a clearing account called Income Summary
questions.explain: Income Summary is then closed to the owner's capital (or retained earnings).
questions.evidence: Closing the revenue accounts: transferring the credit balances in the revenue accounts to a clearing account called Income Summary.

options: The amount an employee receives after all taxes and voluntary deductions
The salary promised in the contract
questions.explain: Gross pay is the amount promised before deductions.
questions.evidence: Net Pay: This is the amount an employee receives after all taxes and voluntary deductions have been taken out.

questions.q: According to the IRS, what is an accounting method?
options: A set of rules used to determine when and how income and expenses are reported
questions.explain: The two most common are the cash and accrual methods.
questions.evidence: An accounting method is a set of rules used to determine when and how income and expenses are reported.

questions.q: What is one of the first things to do when you start a business, for good records?
questions.explain: Separating business and personal money makes records clear and supportable.
questions.evidence: One of the first things you should do when you start a business is open a business checking account.
